headline: High: Aider’s shared-git writes can conflict with Botpress workflows; prompt-injection and leakage are otherwise limited by Botpress’s no-egress profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider can read/write repo files and uses shared git state, so malicious content in files it edits could be copied into outputs. Botpress has no documented filesystem or message-queue bridge here, so the pairwise injection path is indirect and likely manual rather than automatic.
conditions: IF Botpress content is manually pasted into Aider prompts or repo files, injected instructions can influence Aider edits.
IF a shared workspace is added later, file-based prompt injection becomes more plausible.
mitigations: Keep Botpress outputs out of repo files unless reviewed.
Use a strict prompt template that strips instructions from pasted content.
Review Aider diffs before commit.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to any shared artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aider touches source code and git history and can egress broadly, but Botpress is documented with no network egress and no touched data classes. That makes cross-agent leakage limited in this pair as shown, with no evidence Botpress forwards Aider data onward.
conditions: IF Botpress is later configured to ingest the same repo files, Aider edits could be exposed to Botpress.
IF Botpress gains outbound API access, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Do not place secrets in shared repo files.
Keep Botpress isolated from the code workspace.
Audit any manual copy-paste between tools.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace ACLs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aider has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and shared git-repo state across instances; Botpress is not documented as read-only and can install packages. Even without explicit Botpress write paths, the shared mutable repo makes concurrent edits and git-state races dangerous by default for Aider, with uncertainty about Botpress escalating rather than reducing severity.
conditions: IF Botpress writes to the same repository or working tree, concurrent modification conflicts can corrupt state.
IF both agents operate on the same git branch without locking, commits can race.
mitigations: Use separate branches per agent.
Pause one agent while the other commits.
Run a pre-commit diff check before merging.
requires-engineering: add file-level locking or orchestration locks.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aider produces code changes and git commits that Botpress could treat as authoritative if its workflow consumes those outputs, but Botpress has no documented downstream action authority here. The pathway exists through shared artifacts, yet verification is not shown, so this is a default-possible but not proven high-risk cascade.
conditions: IF Botpress ingests Aider-generated files without validation, incorrect code or notes can propagate.
IF Botpress triggers support responses from Aider output, errors can be amplified.
mitigations: Require human review of Aider outputs before Botpress uses them.
Add a validation step for any generated artifacts.
Limit Botpress to read-only consumption of reviewed files.
requires-engineering: implement schema validation between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Aider explicitly handles model-provider API keys and source code/git history, while Botpress’s profile shows no touched data classes or residency/compliance commitments. The only concrete compliance issue visible is Aider’s external model-provider calls; Botpress is not cited because no matching compliance surface is documented.
conditions: IF source code or secrets are sent through Aider to external model providers, policy review is required.
IF Botpress later receives regulated data, a separate residency/compliance assessment is needed.
mitigations: Avoid sending secrets in prompts.
Use approved model-provider accounts only.
Review retention settings for provider APIs.
requires-engineering: document data-flow and residency controls.
